correctness.rationale: Uniform Gaussian inversion gives eta*G -> Q on the compact square. A positive-definite 2-by-2 noise correlation matrix yields strict convexity of Q and its only candidate maximizing vertices; comparing 2M^2/(1+rho) and M^2/(1-rho^2) proves the universal threshold. For the Brownian bridge, m(t)=t(1-t)/2 and all reflected pairs have exact gain (1-d^2)^2/[16(1-d+2eta(1+rho))], strictly beaten by the endpoint/midpoint gain if 2eta(1+rho)(2rho-1)>1. The rational witness eta=1,rho=3/4 has gains 1/44 and at most 1/56. Standalone symbolic and rational checks reproduced these identities; finite checks are not treated as infinite proofs.

value.rationale: The exact universal correlation half-boundary changes high-noise globally optimal placement between a repeat maximum-signal observation and an otherwise uninformative noise-calibration location, independent of the specific continuous kernel. The finite-noise Brownian-bridge rational witness forbids every reflected optimal design and quantifies the gain. This is a physically interpretable sensor-geometry effect, not a known-table recomputation or a numerical coincidence; the claim expressly excludes the full finite-eta phase diagram.
